# Stage 4 implementation plan and audit

Before changing existing files, the 143-file Stage 3 state was hashed and archived in `reports/stage4/frozen_stage3.zip`. `baseline_freeze.json` records exact code/configuration, dataset `multihop-vector-v1`, model/build identities, and historical metrics. `graph_snapshot.json` records the real source/run/domain/embedding state and its SHA-256. Stage 3 reports, runtime modules, extraction, registry, datasets and grader will remain unchanged. Shared API wiring, additive graph settings, docs and the expected API route list are explicit integration changes.

The audit read Stage 1–3 reports, schema/source/evaluation notes, existing gold format, registry aliases/context, ingestion publication, extraction proof validation, and vector runtime/grading. Facts use five approved directed types; MENTIONS/PART_OF/DERIVED_FROM are structural and never reasoning hops. Curated facts have immutable fixture fingerprints and source snapshots. Automatic facts have stable source/span/version IDs, candidate JSON, exact quote/offset/hash, and `verified_rule`; eligibility additionally requires current ready source/run publication and the current processing version. Confidence is not proof.

The reviewed registry has 27 canonical entities and explicit type-aware aliases/context. Plain Priya and Lee Chen are ambiguous. Atlas and Atlas East, and their PostgreSQL instances, are distinct. The 76 Stage 3 benchmark extension documents introduce identities outside that registry; their intended factual chains are not available as accepted graph edges. Do not expand the registry or manufacture facts from held-out labels to improve the comparison. Missing extraction/linking coverage must remain visible, even if graph benchmark accuracy is zero.

1. Add a separate graph runtime package: strict plans, deterministic supported question grammar, exact registry linking with explicit contexts/status, and graph-only responses. Do not import vector retrieval or evaluation keys.
2. Generate only closed-enum Cypher templates for exact one-/two-/three-hop sequences and directions. Start with an indexed canonical ID; bound candidates, answer count, source payloads and query/request time. Overflow abstains rather than selecting the first result.
3. Validate every actual Neo4j edge and endpoint. Check immutable curated payloads against the trusted source contract; rederive automatic proof using the existing Stage 2 validator, verify complete current chunks and structural provenance, and recheck source/edge state before responding. Aggregate independent supports without creating shortcut edges.
4. Select complete validated paths deterministically. Singular conflicting canonical answers abstain; explicitly plural questions may return the complete bounded answer set. Preserve alternatives for review and never answer from partial paths.
5. Add the graph API/CLI with safe infrastructure failures and request IDs. Use a frozen source manifest, not embedding/index dependencies, to define the same approved corpus.
6. Freeze graph parser/retrieval code before evaluation. Reuse the unchanged Stage 3 grader, document curated-to-automatic source normalization, compare on all 122 frozen questions, and keep every failure/abstention. Report parser, linker, extraction, traversal and provenance causes separately. Demonstrate valid paths and active-query latency separately on the existing domain; do not mix those examples into benchmark accuracy.
7. Use real isolated Neo4j adversarial tests for graph mutations, plus all Stage 1–3 regressions. Verify no vector search is called, actual API outage/recovery, repeat evaluation determinism, frozen file hashes, and an unchanged graph snapshot. Publish requested docs/evidence and stop before Stage 5.
